intro: A four-character idiom (四字熟語) packs a whole situation into one noun, and is mostly used as a verdict on how things turned out: ～は一石二鳥だ, 三日坊主で終わる. Choose it by the shape of the situation, not by translating the characters, and learn its reading as a block, because several use unexpected readings (十人十色 is じゅうにんといろ).

skills.rule: Match the shape of the story: one act with two gains 一石二鳥, trouble you caused yourself 自業自得, quitting soon 三日坊主, people differ 十人十色, a meeting that won't come again 一期一会.
skills.explain:
Effort: 一生懸命 (いっしょうけんめい) 'with all one's might', used as an adverb or na-adjective: 一生懸命働く. It does not mean 'lifelong'. 四苦八苦 (しくはっく) 'struggle hard', with する. 試行錯誤 (しこうさくご) 'trial and error': 試行錯誤を重ねる. 三日坊主 (みっかぼうず) 'someone who quits soon': 三日坊主で終わる.

Outcomes: 一石二鳥 (いっせきにちょう) 'two birds with one stone', with だ. 自業自得 (じごうじとく) 'you brought it on yourself', a critical comment on a bad result.

People: 十人十色 (じゅうにんといろ) 'everyone is different'. 以心伝心 (いしんでんしん) 'understanding without words'. 一期一会 (いちごいちえ) 'treasure this meeting, it will not come again'. 半信半疑 (はんしんはんぎ) 'half in doubt', usually 半信半疑で or 半信半疑だった.
patterns: 一生懸命(に) [verb] — do with all one's might
[plan] は 一石二鳥だ — two gains from one act
[taste / opinion] は 十人十色だ — everyone differs
一期一会を大切にする — treasure a one-time meeting
[bad result] は 自業自得だ — you brought it on yourself
[task] に 四苦八苦する — struggle hard
以心伝心で分かる — understand without words
三日坊主で終わる — give up after a short while
半信半疑で [聞く / 試す] — half-believing
試行錯誤を重ねる / 試行錯誤する — trial and error

examples.jp: 毎日[まいにち]{一生懸命[いっしょうけんめい]}練習[れんしゅう]しています。
examples.en: I practise as hard as I can every day.

examples.jp: 好[この]みは{十人十色[じゅうにんといろ]}ですから、正解[せいかい]はありません。
examples.en: Everyone's tastes are different, so there is no right answer.

examples.jp: 日記[にっき]を始[はじ]めたが、{三日坊主[みっかぼうず]}で終[お]わった。
examples.en: I started a diary, but gave up after a few days.

examples.jp: 新[あたら]しい仕事[しごと]に慣[な]れるまで、{四苦八苦[しくはっく]}した。
examples.en: I really struggled until I got used to the new job.

examples.jp: 自転車[じてんしゃ]で通勤[つうきん]すれば、運動[うんどう]になってお金[かね]も節約[せつやく]できるから{一石二鳥[いっせきにちょう]}だ。
examples.en: Cycling to work gives you exercise and saves money: two birds with one stone.

examples.jp: {試行錯誤[しこうさくご]}を重[かさ]ねて、新[あたら]しい商品[しょうひん]ができた。
examples.en: After a lot of trial and error, the new product was ready.

contrast.vs: 一石二鳥 ↔ 自業自得
contrast.note: Both judge an outcome. 一石二鳥 is a happy double gain from one act; 自業自得 is a deserved bad result, often said of someone else.

contrast.vs: 以心伝心 ↔ 一期一会
contrast.note: 以心伝心 is people who understand each other without words (長年の夫婦は以心伝心だ). 一期一会 is valuing a single meeting that will not be repeated.

contrast.vs: 三日坊主 ↔ 試行錯誤
contrast.note: 三日坊主 gives up early. 試行錯誤 keeps going through failure until it works.

mistakes.bad: 遊[あそ]んでばかりで試験[しけん]に落[お]ちたのは{三日坊主[みっかぼうず]}だ。
mistakes.good: 遊[あそ]んでばかりで試験[しけん]に落[お]ちたのは{自業自得[じごうじとく]}だ。
mistakes.note: A bad result of your own behaviour is 自業自得. 三日坊主 is giving something up after a short while.

mistakes.bad: 最初[さいしょ]は彼[かれ]の話[はなし]を{以心伝心[いしんでんしん]}で聞[き]いた。
mistakes.good: 最初[さいしょ]は彼[かれ]の話[はなし]を{半信半疑[はんしんはんぎ]}で聞[き]いた。
mistakes.note: Listening while only half believing is 半信半疑. 以心伝心 is understanding without words.

mistakes.bad: 旅先[たびさき]での出会[であ]いは{十人十色[じゅうにんといろ]}だから、大切[たいせつ]にしたい。
mistakes.good: 旅先[たびさき]での出会[であ]いは{一期一会[いちごいちえ]}だから、大切[たいせつ]にしたい。
mistakes.note: A meeting to treasure because it won't happen again is 一期一会. 十人十色 says that people differ.

skills.tip: Sum up the story in three English words (two gains, own fault, quit early ...) and pick the idiom that says exactly that.
